title: Analyst shared definitions
description: Shared enums and ids for analyst turns (ADR 0047). Definition library only.

datasetId.title: Dataset id
datasetId.description: Core-minted id of a dataset produced in an analyst turn (prefix ds_). Never invented by the model.

abilityId.title: Analyst ability
abilityId.description: One independently switchable ability. Model strength never enables these; each is off unless every level allows it and the controller is analyst_capable where required.

sourceLabel.title: Claim source label
sourceLabel.description: Where a claim or number comes from. app: verified read fact. computed: derived fact with provenance. web: cited fetched page. knowledge: model general knowledge (never the tenant's own figures).

dataClass.title: Field data class
dataClass.description: Sensitivity of a dataset field. Same ladder as RAG: public < internal < confidential < restricted. restricted never leaves for an external model; local compute may still use it.

reasonCode.title: Analyst reason code
reasonCode.description: Typed reason for an analyst refusal or fallback. Carried on DialogueDirective.reason_code when it is also a common ErrCode, or in details.analyst_reason when more specific. Mirror of common error codes plus analyst-specific codes listed in common/error.

progressStage.title: Analyst progress stage
progressStage.description: Stable progress stage ids emitted as TurnEvent progress.stage during an analyst turn (additive values on the turn-event enum).

domainClassification.title: Domain classification
domainClassification.description: Model-judged classification of the user message against the application package assistant.domain. Typed; out_of_domain refuses without search or read.

roundingMode.title: Numeric rounding mode
roundingMode.description: How the core rounds derived numbers before they become facts the verifier accepts. half_up is the default.

numberFormat.title: Accepted number presentation
numberFormat.description: Forms the verifier accepts as equal to a fact value. The core normalises before compare; the model may use any listed form.
